question: How do we reconcile the hadiths on strangeness and the 73 sects with the hadiths on Muslim unity?
asked: Our Prophet ﷺ said in a hadith that Islam began as something strange and it shall return to something strange, so give glad tidings to the strangers. And our Prophet ﷺ also told us that his ummah will divide into 73 groups. So how do we reconcile the hadith of strangeness and the hadith of splitting with the hadiths about Muslim unity?
answer:
We seem to have a little bit of a, maybe, internal tension, where it seems as if one hadith is predicting differentiation, one hadith is saying that people will be strange, Muslims will be strange, and so many hadith are telling us to be united.

So with this we say that if you look at the commentary of this hadith, if you look at what Ibn Hajar said, as-San'ani said, ash-Shawkani said, they all mentioned that this hadith of the 73 is actually one of the most misunderstood and misused and abused hadith. People use it to try to foment factionalism, and that was never the goal of our Prophet ﷺ. Our Prophet ﷺ never intended that we go and disunite even more than is already happening.

So what we need to do is to look at the goal of this hadith and the wording of this hadith. The hadith of the 73 sects is a hasan hadith; it's not sahih. It is hasan, it's a good hadith. It's found in Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah and others. The most authentic hadith, by the way, the ones in Bukhari and Muslim, they don't mention 73. They simply say there shall be a group that will be rightly guided until Judgment Day. So they mention some positive thing. And that is why some of our scholars, a small minority, have said that this hadith of 73 is actually not authentic. However, inshallah, the majority position, the correct position, is that it is authentic.

However, if you look at the wording of the hadith, the hadith begins, "My ummah shall disunite, my ummah shall split up into 73." This wording is so important. Why? Because the Prophet ﷺ begins the hadith by stressing "my ummah." Then he mentions it will be divided. So all of these groups, without exception, are within the fold of Islam. And if they are within the fold of Islam, this means that the rights of the Muslim, the haqq al-Muslim, shall be given to all of them: in terms of responding to the salam, in terms of making du'a for them, in terms of visiting them when they are sick, in terms of praying janazah over them. So the rights of the ummah will be given to all of these groups.

We are not talking about those groups that are outside the fold of Islam. When are the groups outside the fold of Islam? When they contradict the explicit kalimah, la ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad rasul Allah, or they contravene something that is known by unanimous opinion: everybody knows it, and a group says, "We're not going to accept this." And these are the exception. So within the ummah, there will be some division.

Also, as-San'ani says it is a big misunderstanding to say that the majority of the ummah will be misguided. They get this from the fraction, 72 out of 73. But as-San'ani himself says, and before him Ibn Hajar, that all of these other groups put together are a small percentage of the one correct group. All of the other groups will not be as large as the mainstream ummah.

How do we know this? Because our Prophet ﷺ predicted that the bulk of the ummah shall be rightly guided: "My ummah is a blessed ummah that Allah has shown mercy to." Our Prophet ﷺ mentioned that Jibreel showed him the ummah that will go to heaven, and it blocked the entire horizon. Our Prophet ﷺ said, and the hadith is in Bukhari, "Would you like it that out of all of the 70-plus ummahs, my ummah will be one third of the people of Jannah?" They said, "Allahu akbar, one third." He said, "Would you like it if the fraction was one half?" They said, "Allahu akbar, one half." He said, "Wallahi, I'm optimistic that my ummah shall be two thirds of the people of Jannah." One ummah out of so many ummahs, and two thirds!

This means that the majority of the ummah is, inshallah, rightly guided, not incorrectly guided. It is a mistake to say that the majority is incorrectly guided. In fact, one of the hallmarks of orthodoxy is the mainstream. Our Prophet ﷺ said, "Hold on to the mainstream. The blessings of Allah, the hand of Allah, is over the jama'ah." So the bulk of the ummah, alhamdulillah, is rightly guided.

And we know this from the theological beliefs. The bulk of the ummah believes in the Qur'an, believes in the Sunnah, respects the Sahabah, the hadith of Jibreel, the six arkan. They believe in them. This is, alhamdulillah, the majority. As for the disagreements beyond this, inshallah, this is not something we should make a big deal over.

And as for those who disagree with the six fundamental pillars of iman: so there are groups that don't like the Sahabah, there are groups that reject Qadr. These deviations do not kick them outside the fold of Islam. They remain Muslim. Therefore, they have some connection with us, but not as strong as the connection of those that obviously fulfill all six of the pillars.

As well, how we treat these other groups varies from time to time and place to place and situation to situation. At times of weakness, we need to strengthen ourselves by unifying as much as possible. Perhaps at times of 'izzah and power, we can be more harsh with those who are deviating. But at times of weakness, these are the times where we do not disunite; we attempt to unite. And this is something that our classical scholars, including Ibn Taymiyyah and others, have mentioned.

So the bottom line: **the ahadith of the 73 and the ahadith of being strange at the end of times are authentic, but we should not use these ahadith to increase division.** That's not the intent of our Prophet.

As for the ahadith of strangeness, it has nothing to do with division. It has everything to do with sticking to morality, sticking to good akhlaq when people have left akhlaq. Because our Prophet ﷺ said that towards the end of times, the one who holds on to the religion will be like the one who's holding on to burning charcoal, burning fuel. He didn't say that within the ummah there's going to be division. He said, in the hadith of the strangeness, people will not be following Islam. So the one who is honest, the one who is praying five times a day, the one who is avoiding the major sins, that person will be strange. And that is true. So it has nothing to do with unity and disunity. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best.
